text:
olivia: Heads-up — after enabling INT8 kernels on dedicated for gpt-13B we’re seeing 12–25% tail latency regressions at seq=1024. avg throughput looks similar but 95p and 99p shifted. putting this here to triage. link to flame: https://perf/reports/1768123456/flame
marc: I see that on staging too. throughput ~same but tails worse. my initial suspect is calibration distribution changed -> different dynamic ranges -> different kernel selection path (we fall back to slower xmm kernel on some ops).
juan: can you paste the calibration config you used? per-channel or per-tensor? sample size?
olivia: config snippet:
```
calibration: {
  method: "kl",
  granularity: "per-tensor",
  sample_count: 1024,
  outlier_clip: 0.999,
  two_pass: false
}
```
log snippet:
```
[run] quantize_kernel: int8_vnni selected for qkv; fallback: int8_slow_conv for attention_ffn on some layers
[metrics] seq=1024 batch=8 avg_tok/s 5200 -> baseline 6300 (−17%)
```
priya: per-tensor tends to be faster on our fused kernels since per-channel kernels aren't vectorized in our CUDA paths. but per-tensor can worsen dynamic range. curious why it picks slow conv fallback — that implies outliers exceeded threshold on some weight groups.
dennis: right — fallback happens when quant params would overflow lanes or when we don't have a per-channel kernel implemented for that op + hardware path. in those cases planner picks an alternate implementation (slower).
sasha: Two quick hypotheses: 1) calibration sample set has heavy-tail outliers pushing scale up; 2) switching to per-channel removes need for fallback but may change accuracy. We should try percentile clipping (0.9995 or 0.9999) and two-pass sampling (warmup to prime KV / activations then measure).
juan: agree. also we should verify KV cache access pattern changes under quantized kernels — if cache hits move or cache warmup differs, effective latency can spike. can we repro with a replay harness using real traces?
olivia: started a perf job: run id perf-1768123456-a with three arms: (A) per-tensor KL 1024/0.999, (B) per-channel KL 1024/0.999, (C) per-channel KL 2048 + clip 0.9999 + two_pass. deploy-bot will post results.
deploy-bot: perf job perf-1768123456-a queued -> http://ci/perf/perf-1768123456-a (ETA ~18m) :hourglass:
marc: small note — when you run per-channel, we must ensure we use the new int8_pc kernels (they are guarded by planner flag --use-int8-pc). otherwise planner will still choose slow fallback. add `--planner-flag=use-int8-pc=true` to the perf job.
olivia: added the flag for B/C. also attaching a tiny repro harness command:
```bash
./tools/replay_trace --trace traces/session-2026-02-21.json --model gpt-13b --calib-config calib.yaml --planner-flag use-int8-pc=true --batch 8 --seq 1024
```
priya: for outliers we have two approaches: percentile clipping + do not quantize top-k percent of activations; or sample weighting (downweight long-tail examples). both need eval against our quality prompts. quality vs perf tradeoff.
dennis: can someone run a cheap ablation: turn off clip -> run 100 samples -> dump quant params and count layers that go to fallback path. that will show if outliers are the primary cause.
sasha: FYI we already saw one regression case where per-channel reduced perp by 0.8 but latency increased because a custom attention kernel didn't have per-channel implementation. so outcome depends on kernel coverage matrix. we should add kernel coverage telemetry to perf dashboard.
juan: proposal for triage steps (short):
  1) reproduce with replay_trace and the three arms (A/B/C).
  2) collect planner decision log + kernel names per-op + quant params per-layer.
  3) run fallback-count ablation (dennis's idea).
  4) run quality eval on standard prompts for arms A/C to check regression.
olivia: awesome. I'll kick off the runs and paste results. timeline: perf job completes in ~18m, then we run ablation (~30m). prioritize 95/99p and planner logs.
marc: small reminder: ensure we pin GPU driver to 535.x in these runs — some kernels behave differently across drivers.
priya: also test with a smaller batch (4) — batching heuristics can amplify fallback overhead if per-request batching surface changes.
dennis: happy to instrument planner logs for the ablation. will add a small tracer that emits: {op,layer,chosen_impl,quant_granularity,scale,max_abs} for each op.
sasha: thumbs-up. also add a column for KV cache hit rate pre/post quant — we want to see if quant kernels affect cache alignment or offsets.
olivia: thanks all — will post perf links & raw planner logs when available. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: perf job perf-1768123456-a finished -> http://ci/perf/perf-1768123456-a/results (A: 95p +22% vs baseline, B: 95p +3%, C: 95p +1%)
olivia: quick summary from results: A (per-tensor) is worst; B (per-channel) mostly fixes tail but planner still chose fallback on 2 conv layers; C (per-channel + larger sample + clip + two_pass) matched baseline latency but added small quality delta (~0.2% token-level).
juan: that points to two wins: per-channel + clip + two-pass sampling. quality delta seems acceptable but we need more eval on long-tail prompts.
marc: ok next steps: ship planner flag default to enable use-int8-pc only when kernel coverage >= 95% OR when calib config includes per-channel+clip. open PR to impl telemetry and add guidance in docs.
priya: will prepare a short runbook: recommended calib config for INT8 on prod (per-channel, sample_count >= 2048, clip 0.9999, two_pass true) and fallbacks to revert to per-tensor if kernel coverage low.
olivia: perfect. closing the loop once runbook + PR merged. thanks everyone.
